Requirement Statement: The firmware shall enable a hardware watchdog such that, if the control task becomes unresponsive during the automatic sequence, the MCU resets and returns the system to the boot safe state.
Source Text / Evidence:
• PWM is disabled automatically after the run completes.
• The motor remains stopped after the sequence until reset or power-cycle.
- An active STSPIN830 EN/FAULT condition shall immediately disable PWM at any time.
Inference Rationale: The demo runs unattended with no UART control; a deadlock could leave PWM enabled and prevent the required automatic shutdown and post-run stop state. A hardware watchdog is necessary to guarantee recovery to a known safe state if firmware becomes unresponsive.
Acceptance Criteria: Introduce a deliberate software hang during the 8–18 s hold window; verify that a watchdog-induced reset occurs and, after reset, PWM remains disabled for the 3 s boot delay before any attempt to enable the driver.
Preconditions: Firmware becomes unresponsive during any phase of the automatic sequence.
Postconditions / Expected Behavior: MCU resets via watchdog; system re-enters the 0–3 s safe boot state with PWM disabled and driver in standby.
Failure Behavior: If a hang occurs and no reset follows, or PWM remains enabled, declare safety noncompliance and halt further operation.

Requirement Statement: Following detection of an active STSPIN830 EN/FAULT condition, the firmware shall not attempt to re-enable the motor driver or PWM automatically; recovery shall require a reset or power-cycle.
Source Text / Evidence:
- An active STSPIN830 EN/FAULT condition shall immediately disable PWM at any time.
After 20 s
Disable PWM, place driver in standby, and remain stopped until reset/power cycle.
Inference Rationale: The PRD mandates immediate PWM disable on fault but is silent on auto-retry. Automatic re-enables can cause repeated torque transients and conflict with the stated expectation that the system remains stopped until a reset/power-cycle after completion; extending the same stop-until-reset rule to fault cases prevents unsafe oscillation.
Acceptance Criteria: Assert EN/FAULT during the run to stop PWM; then clear EN/FAULT without resetting and observe for a period ≥ the demo duration that the driver remains in standby and no PWM is generated until a manual reset/power-cycle.
Preconditions: EN/FAULT becomes active at any time during the sequence.
Postconditions / Expected Behavior: PWM remains disabled and driver stays in standby until a reset or power-cycle occurs.
Failure Behavior: If firmware re-enables PWM/driver without a reset after a fault, declare safety noncompliance and halt further operation.

Requirement Statement: The firmware shall complete TIM1 and PWM GPIO configuration with PWM outputs disabled before asserting the motor driver enable at the start of the sequence.
Source Text / Evidence:
- Configure TIM1 to generate three-phase PWM.
3-8 s
Enable driver and ramp electrical frequency from 1 Hz to 10 Hz. Ramp PWM amplitude from 10% to 20%.
Inference Rationale: Enabling the driver before PWM and GPIO are fully configured risks undefined input levels and unintended torque, which would violate the required safe boot window and smooth startup ramps. Ordering the bring-up makes the stated behavior achievable and verifiable.
Acceptance Criteria: On an oscilloscope, confirm that prior to the EN rising edge at t≈3 s, U/V/W show no switching activity; immediately after EN is asserted and PWM is enabled, the first active duty cycle equals the specified initial 10% and ramps per the sequence.
Preconditions: Boot delay has elapsed and no EN/FAULT is active.
Postconditions / Expected Behavior: Driver is enabled only after PWM/GPIO are configured and idle; startup ramps then proceed from the defined initial conditions.
Failure Behavior: If driver EN asserts before PWM/GPIO configuration is complete, immediately deassert EN, keep PWM disabled, and abort the sequence.

Requirement Statement: On any MCU reset event (including initial boot), the firmware shall keep PWM disabled and the motor driver in standby for the first 3 seconds before any enable action may occur.
Source PRD Section: Validation Criteria (p. 2); Automatic Test Sequence (p. 1); After 20 s (p. 2)
Acceptance Criteria: Measure U/V/W from t=0 to t=3 s after any reset (power-on, external reset, watchdog timeout, or brown-out): no PWM switching is observed and the driver EN is deasserted (standby asserted). After t≥3 s, enabling actions may proceed per sequence if no EN/FAULT is active.
Preconditions: A reset occurs (power-on, external reset, watchdog timeout, or brown-out).
Postconditions / Expected Behavior: From reset to t=3 s, PWM remains disabled and driver is in standby; sequence may restart after t≥3 s if no fault is present.
Failure Behavior: If any PWM activity is detected before 3 s or the driver cannot be held in standby, keep PWM disabled, deassert EN, and do not start the sequence; flag noncompliance.
